card.name: Linking words before adverse-event or timing phrases
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (comma, 'of', 'after', 'may', 'reactions') that come right before an expected adverse-effect or stopping/starting-time phrase in drug-label text.

modes.label: Before adverse reactions
modes.description: Words in 'potential for serious adverse reactions' or 'risk of psychiatric adverse reactions' that lead into a harm term.
modes.example: Because of the potential for serious adverse<< reactions>> in nursing infants from chlorthal

modes.label: After starting or stopping a drug
modes.description: The word 'after' or a comma following a mention of starting, stopping, or vomiting after a dose.
modes.example: If vomiting occurs immediately<< after>> taking a dose of ROZLYT

modes.label: Risk statements
modes.description: Verbs or 'of' linking a therapy to an associated risk.
modes.example: PPI therapy<< may>> be associated with increased risk.

card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in label sentences that are about to name a side effect or a timing after a drug.
